doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Ellington as favorite, Basie's genuine character
summary: Wolff ranks Ellington first, praises Count Basie's unchanged character from Bennie Moten days to wealth, and calls Ellington the best American composer.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Is Basie is personal favorite of yours? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Well Ellington is number one. I think Duke Ellington, well you heard Basie in the films yesterday agree with that comment. I think Basie, and I met Count Basie a number of times personally. I think on a personal level he was the most genuine. He was the nicest. Success never went to the head of Bill Basie. He was the same, I think, when he was getting started with Bennie Moten and probably didn’t have two nickels to rub together, as in the latter part of his life when he was a very wealthy, successful man. It just didn’t go to his head. He didn’t get what we in the legal profession call “phrentolitis.” Perhaps that can’t be said for lots of others. But when I think of American original art form music, Duke Ellington is at the top of my list. Count Basie certainly isn’t far behind.
Right. Who is a better American composer than Duke Ellington?
